sections.h2: How do Johns Creek owners usually sell their homes?
sections.html:
Most go through a broker listing, some negotiate directly with a buyer, and a smaller group takes an investor's cash bid. The deciding factors are the calendar and the shape of the house. Johns Creek lies in northeastern Fulton County, so the tax bills and recording steps involve Fulton County as well as the city.

A broker listing fits a house that photographs well, since it reaches the biggest group of buyers, at the price of staging, inspections and a lender's appraisal. Negotiating directly saves the commission and hands every task to you. An investor's cash bid gives up price in return for speed and certainty.

  • Highest price: a prepared listing, ideally with a broker who knows your subdivision and school zone.
  • Most control: a direct sale, if contracts and disclosures do not worry you.
  • Fastest or easiest: an investor bid on a house with condition problems.

Whatever you choose, assemble the deed, the newest Fulton County tax bill, any homeowner association papers and the permits for work done on the house. Permit history is easy to retrieve because the city issues permits through an online portal.

sections.h2: What do federal numbers show about Johns Creek homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate for Johns Creek is 80,401 people, and four of every five homes are lived in by their owners, 80.4 percent for 2020-2024. The midpoint home value is $629,400.

With that many owner-occupied homes, a typical Johns Creek sale is one resident handing a lived-in house to another family. Households average 2.82 people, so the family-sized house is the usual comparison.

sections.h2: What makes Johns Creek different from nearby suburbs?
sections.html:
Johns Creek is a young city. It incorporated on December 1, 2006, after a July 2006 referendum in northeast Fulton County, and the city says it is now the 10th largest in Georgia. It covers about 32 square miles roughly 25 miles north of Atlanta.

The city's own history page traces the area to trading posts on the Chattahoochee River in the early 19th century and to Technology Park/Johns Creek, a mixed-use business park that began in 1981 along McGinnis Ferry Road and Medlock Bridge Road. Today the city reports that about 25 percent of residents are international, with India, China and South Korea the largest groups. Recreation and Parks maintains more than 400 acres of parkland and nature reserve, with five access points to the Chattahoochee River.

The city also points to outside rankings it has earned: it says U.S. News & World Report named it the best place to live in the U.S. in 2025 and listed it first for safety. Treat those as the city's claims, and let the house itself carry your listing.

  • Mail can carry a Johns Creek address with any of five ZIP codes: 30005, 30022, 30024, 30076 or 30097.
  • The city does not run garbage collection, so residents contract with private haulers.
  • Water comes through Fulton County, and power through Georgia Power or Sawnee Electric.
  • Police and fire service come from the city's own departments.

Buyers ask about those basics, so have the answers ready. A mailing address can carry a neighboring city's name, so buyers should confirm the property is inside Johns Creek with the city's address tool.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Johns Creek homes?
sections.html:
Fulton County Schools serves Johns Creek. The city's schools page says 19 Fulton County public elementary, middle and high schools serve residents, and which one a child attends depends on the address and the attendance zone.

Eleven Fulton County elementary schools and one charter school serve the city, with names such as Abbotts Hill, Barnwell, Dolvin, Findley Oaks, Medlock Bridge, Ocee, Shakerag, State Bridge Crossing and Wilson Creek. Some of the elementary schools carry Roswell or Alpharetta mailing addresses even though they serve Johns Creek families. Four private schools also list themselves as serving the city: Holy Redeemer Catholic School, Mount Pisgah Christian School, Perimeter School and Woodward Academy North.

Zoning is address-specific, so do not tell a buyer which school a house feeds without checking. Direct buyers to Fulton County Schools to confirm the current zone for the exact address.

sections.h2: Where does a Johns Creek tax bill come from?
sections.html:
Johns Creek owners owe tax to Fulton County, which includes the school system, and to the City of Johns Creek, and the Fulton County Tax Commissioner mails the bill. The city's new-resident FAQ says so directly.

The Fulton County Board of Assessors sets the value and mails the Notice of Assessment each year. The 2026 appeal period gave most owners until July 31, 2026, and that date has passed. Homeowners who qualified for a 2026 homestead exemption but missed the April 1 filing date could apply during that appeal period, and anyone who bought after January 1 applies for the 2027 tax year. Fulton County also says each notice now shows estimated tax savings, with discounts and exemptions, in place of an estimated tax figure.

  • Search your parcel on the Fulton assessor's site to verify the exemptions on record.
  • Ask the Fulton County Tax Commissioner whether the current bill is paid.
  • Have your closing attorney show how this year's tax is shared with the new owner.

sections.h2: What permits and code rules affect a Johns Creek sale?
sections.html:
Johns Creek runs building permits through an online customer self-service portal, and its permit process has six steps: application, fee payment, plan review, permit issued, required inspections and permit completed. The city also posts a Do I Need a Permit checklist.

If you finished a basement, built a deck or replaced a major system without a permit, a buyer's inspection may find it. The city's Code Compliance Division enforces the local ordinances and property maintenance code, and the nuisance and zoning ordinances are posted on its code regulations page. Ask Community Development whether any permit on your address is still open and close it out before you list.

Recording the deed also triggers Georgia's transfer tax. Check the contract to see which side pays.

sections.h2: When does an investor's bid make sense in Johns Creek?
sections.html:
An investor's bid is worth a look when you cannot or will not prepare the house for retail buyers. Houses here carry high values, and a dated or damaged one can sit while carrying costs keep running.

  • An estate house whose heirs live elsewhere.
  • Deferred maintenance that would not survive a buyer's inspection.
  • A relocation with a short fuse.
  • Past work done without a permit.

Request any bid in writing, see which closing charges are yours, and set it beside a listing broker's net estimate.

faqs.q: Do Johns Creek owners pay both city and county tax?
faqs.a: Yes, the city's FAQ says Fulton County, including the school system, and the City of Johns Creek each tax the property, and the Fulton County Tax Commissioner sends the bill.

faqs.q: Is a Johns Creek mailing address always inside the city?
faqs.a: Not always. Johns Creek shares the ZIP codes 30005, 30022, 30024, 30076 and 30097 with neighboring cities, and the city offers an address lookup tool for confirmation.

faqs.q: Who hauls trash at a Johns Creek house?
faqs.a: A private company does. The city says it provides no garbage collection, so residents contract on their own, and a buyer will ask which hauler serves the house.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Fulton County appeal window still open?
faqs.a: No for most owners. The 2026 deadline was July 31, 2026 unless the notice printed another date. An appeal challenges the value, not the tax amount.

faqs.q: Which side pays Georgia's transfer tax on a Johns Creek sale?
faqs.a: State law makes the seller liable, though contracts often move the cost to the buyer. It must be paid before the deed is recorded.
